//: FRONTEND-BFF.md §7 — a member of the workspace above, which owns the only lockfile.
THIS IS THE KIT the root package.json said would arrive 'when the second app
arrives': @ab-ovo/mcp is that second app, and it has been reaching one file into
@ab-ovo/app (src/content.ts, 'the only file in this package that reaches into
@ab-ovo/app') since it was written. That file said what would move on the day this
package existed — see its own header, now out of date on purpose until this commit
updates it too. Docs updated in the same commit: docs/architecture/MCP-SERVER-SKETCH.md
§6, this package.json's own former home in web/package.json and web/mcp/package.json.
WHAT LIVES HERE, and why the line is drawn where it is: the loader (bundle.ts), the
schema types (schema.ts) and the validator that refuses rather than degrades
(validate.ts) — content.ts's own three-part description of what a second consumer
needs, taken literally rather than as a chance to move more. Rendering (maths.ts,
markdown.ts), edition/track selection for the index UI (chosen-edition.ts,
chosen-track.ts) and lab-runtime asset staging (runtime-assets.ts) stay in
@ab-ovo/app: none of them is 'the loader, the validator or the schema types', and
@ab-ovo/mcp needs none of them — it returns the book's own text to a model, never a
rendered page. have-bundle.ts moved too, alongside bundle.ts rather than staying in
@ab-ovo/app: it is loader test infrastructure (skip-locally-refuse-in-CI for the
tests that exercise the real pinned bundle), and leaving it behind would have made
this package's own bundle.test.ts reach BACKWARDS into @ab-ovo/app for it — the one
shape this extraction exists to rule out.
NO RUNTIME DEPENDENCY. bundle.ts, schema.ts, validate.ts and have-bundle.ts import
only node:fs and each other — checked, not assumed, the same standard
REPO-BASELINE.md §4b holds every other package in this workspace to.
SHIPPED AS RAW TypeScript, no build step — @ab-ovo/mcp's own precedent for a package
nothing publishes. `exports` points straight at src/index.ts; Node's type stripping
reads it directly under `node --test`, and @ab-ovo/app's Next build reads it because
it is named in next.config.mjs's `transpilePackages` — webpack/Turbopack only
transpile a workspace package's TypeScript when told to; an untranspiled one fails
the build the first time it is imported, not silently.
Three more `exports` entries hand out raw JSON no barrel should pre-parse:
`./fixtures/*` is @ab-ovo/mcp's content.ts building its unit-tier BundleSource —
validateBundle(fixture) is part of what it is testing, so the fixture must arrive
unvalidated — and @ab-ovo/app's own runtime-assets.test.ts and lab/protocol.test.ts,
which need the same fixture for the same reason, one package over. The two
`content-schema.v*.json` entries are runtime-assets.test.ts's own direct read of the
document validate.ts otherwise reads internally.
